name: DealCloud (Intapp)
verdict: No third-party OAuth app is known; each customer's DealCloud admin creates API credentials (client ID and secret) for their own tenant and sends them to you. Likely days to weeks per customer; low confidence.
needGuide: No — just collect tenant hostname, client ID and secret from each customer admin, but you need a test tenant first.

auth.detail: Likely: OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant against each customer's own DealCloud site (tenant-specific host), using a client ID and secret issued by that customer's admin; short-lived bearer tokens. There is no third-party registered app with authorization-code flow that I know of. Unverified this session.

effort.timeToFirstTest: needs a tenant; 1+ hour once credentials exist
effort.timeToProduction: unknown; per-customer onboarding, likely days to weeks each

approval.gate: No central app approval: each customer admin issues credentials for their own tenant, so every customer needs an admin step. Intapp may offer partner or marketplace routes for a named integration (unverified).

scopes.why: Likely a small scope set; real permissions come from the service user's role in the tenant (unverified).
scopes.summary: Likely a limited scope set (for example data access) with real permissions determined by the service user's role in the tenant. Unverified.

cost: Requires a DealCloud (Intapp) customer tenant; no public sandbox or free tier known

steps.do: Obtain a DealCloud test or sandbox tenant through Intapp or a pilot customer
Customer admin creates API credentials in the tenant and shares client ID, secret and the site hostname
Build a connect form: tenant hostname, client ID, client secret; store encrypted
Request tokens with the client-credentials grant against the tenant token endpoint; refresh on expiry
Validate with a test call, then map customer-specific entries and fields via the schema endpoints
Ask Intapp about a partner or marketplace route if you want a branded integration

roles.team: A solutions or integration engineer who can obtain a sandbox or customer tenant via Intapp or a customer sponsor.
roles.customer: A DealCloud admin must create the API credentials and choose the service user and permissions; customer IT may also need to allow-list your IPs.

testing: Needs a DealCloud tenant, ideally a customer's sandbox or Intapp partner environment (likely).

automation.humanMust: A customer DealCloud admin must issue credentials; a human negotiates tenant access and any Intapp partner agreement.
